testimonials.text: The case-based discussions with real surgical scenarios, like the modifications of the Watson-Jones approach or the trochanteric flip osteotomy, were highly engaging. They allowed me to see practical decision-making in action rather than just theoretical knowledge. I also appreciated the integration of anatomy, surgical technique, and complication management, which helped me understand why each approach is chosen.
The case-based discussions, surgical approach selection, fracture management techniques, and practical tips shared by experienced surgeons were the most interesting aspects of the course.
I found the case based discussions particularly interesting especially how different surgical approaches were compared and justified in real clinical scenarios.

I found the detailed case study discussions and the practical surgical pearls shared by the expert faculty to be the most interesting parts of the course. Learning specific technical workarounds, such as using a precise drill-hole technique when standard power tools aren't accessible, provided highly valuable, real-world clinical insights.

I found the case-based discussions particularly engaging, especially the management of complex femoral neck fractures and combined neck-shaft injuries. The practical insights into decision-making in low-resource settings, implant selection, and techniques like capsulotomy and open reduction were very valuable.
Discussing about the proper choice for implants was an interesting part to cut off the curiosity I had.
